quiz.title: NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Maths Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight harder questions drawn from across the Class 12 syllabus — calculus, matrices and determinants, vectors and 3D, probability and differential equations. Answer each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Mathematics — mixed chapters

questions.q: If ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> x(1−x)<sup>9</sup> dx, its value is:
questions.explanation: Use the beta-style result ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> x<sup>m</sup>(1−x)<sup>n</sup>dx = m! n!/(m+n+1)!. Here m=1, n=9, giving 1!·9!/11! = 1/(10·11) = 1/110.

questions.q: If A is a 3×3 matrix with |A| = 4, then |2A| equals:
questions.explanation: For an n×n matrix, |kA| = k<sup>n</sup>|A|. With n=3, k=2: |2A| = 2<sup>3</sup>·4 = 8·4 = 32.

questions.q: The angle between the vectors a and b where |a|=1, |b|=2 and a·b = 1 is:
The integrating factor of dy/dx + y tan x = sec x is:
questions.explanation: IF = e<sup>∫tan x dx</sup> = e<sup>ln|sec x|</sup> = sec x.

questions.q: A die is thrown twice. The probability that the sum of the numbers is 8, given the first throw is 5, is:
questions.explanation: Given first = 5, the second must be 3 for a sum of 8. With the first fixed, the second is uniform over 6 outcomes, so the conditional probability is 1/6.

questions.q: If the function f(x) = |x−1| + |x−2| is considered on R, the number of points where it is NOT differentiable is:
questions.explanation: A sum of modulus terms has corners at each break point. |x−1| gives a corner at x=1 and |x−2| at x=2, so f is non-differentiable at exactly 2 points.

questions.q: The distance of the point (1, 2, 3) from the plane x + y + z = 3 is:
If A is a square matrix such that A² = A, then (I + A)³ − 7A equals:
questions.explanation: Since A is idempotent, A<sup>n</sup>=A. Expand (I+A)³ = I + 3A + 3A² + A³ = I + 3A + 3A + A = I + 7A. Subtracting 7A leaves I.

faq.q: What are NCERT Exemplar problems and how do they differ from the textbook?
faq.a: The NCERT Exemplar is a separate problem book published by NCERT with higher-order, application-heavy questions — MCQs, fill-in-the-blanks, true/false and long problems. They are tougher than the standard textbook exercises and are widely used to prepare for board exams as well as JEE Main.

faq.q: Which Class 12 chapters carry the most exemplar weight for boards and JEE?
faq.a: Calculus dominates — continuity and differentiability, applications of derivatives, integrals and differential equations together carry the largest share. Matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, and probability round out the high-yield chapters.

faq.q: Is it enough to solve only the NCERT Exemplar for the Class 12 board exam?
faq.a: For the board exam the NCERT textbook exercises are essential and the Exemplar is a strong add-on for the harder problems that appear in longer-mark questions. If you are also targeting JEE Main, the Exemplar is close to a must, since several questions map directly to its style.

faq.q: How should I use exemplar solutions without just copying the answers?
faq.a: Attempt each problem cold first, give it a genuine try, and only then check the worked solution. Focus on the method and the point where you got stuck rather than the final number — that is where exemplar problems teach the most.
